games.title: The Pumpkin Patch
games.description: Spooky silhouettes rise from the pumpkin patch!  Not interactive - just watch and enjoy!
games.how_to_play: Just sit back and watch the spooky silhouettes rise from the pumpkin patch!

games.title: Stack-o'-Lantern
games.credits: Designed and written by Claude Code at John's invitation
games.description: Pumpkin slabs slide across the night sky. Tap to drop each one on the tower. Whatever hangs over the edge gets sliced off, so sloppy drops make the tower narrower until one misses. The moon is judging you.
games.how_to_play: Tap anywhere to drop the sliding pumpkin onto the one below. Line the edges up: a perfect drop keeps the full width, and three perfects in a row grow it back. Stack as many as you can before a slab misses.

games.title: Candy Go Fish
games.credits: Gameplay and candy artwork supplied by John; demo and fish icon by Codex.
games.description: A friendly candy-table showdown with Wendy. Collect three of a kind to claim a set!
games.how_to_play: Select a candy you hold, then tap Got any? A match gives you one candy and another request. Otherwise, tap the pile to fish; drawing always ends your turn. Tell Wendy to Go fish when you have none of her request. Most sets wins when either hand empties or all sets are collected.

what_this_file_is: Halloween 2026 - the list of games. THE ONE PLACE to add, rename, reorder or describe a game.
The app reads this file when it starts and makes one button per game in the bottom panel.
Add a game: put its files in games/<folder_name>/ (with an index.html inside) and add an entry above.
Nothing in app/ ever changes. app.js reads this file; a game designer never edits app.js.
What goes here: anything the player might want while BROWSING games, before tapping one.
Also here: up to three simple on/off switches for your game (see settings below), which the app draws and remembers for you.
Everything else (assets, sizes, any options screen of your own) lives in the game's own folder; the app never reads it.
If the same fact is in both places, this file wins: the app shows what is written here.
JSON cannot hold comments, which is why this _about block exists. The app ignores it.
It sits at the bottom so the data comes first.

fields.folder_name: The game's folder under games/. LOWERCASE ONLY (GitHub Pages is case-sensitive). Required.
fields.goes_in_slot: Where the game appears: "home" for the home game (shown at start, no button), or a whole number 1 to 8 for a fixed cell on the button board. The board is two rows of four: 1 2 3 4 across the upper row, 5 6 7 8 across the lower row. A game always sits in its own cell, so slot 1 is always top left and slot 8 always bottom right; cells nobody uses stay empty. If only one row has games, that row is drawn in the middle. 9 or above, or "", means the game is listed but not shown - an easy way to bench a game. If two entries claim the same slot, the first one in the file wins.
fields.title: The game's full name, shown on its button.
fields.short_title: A short name, about 12 characters at most: shown in the narrow top bar, and on the button when there is no usable icon (the button fits about ten characters per line, two lines). Leave it the same as title if the title is short.
fields.icon: Path to the game's icon, relative to the game's folder, e.g. assets/icon.png. SPEC: a square 256 x 256 real pixels, PNG with a transparent background (or an SVG with a square viewBox). Draw anything that fills the square; it is shown inside an orange rounded button with a small orange margin, so plan for orange around it. Wiggle room: each side may be 200 to 300 pixels and the two sides may differ by up to 10; the app scales it. Outside that, or missing, or a bad path: the button shows short_title as text instead (and says why in the browser console).
fields.designer: Who made the game. Free text.
fields.credits: Where art, sound or ideas came from. Free text, may be empty.
fields.date: When the game was finished or last changed. Free text, for display only.
fields.description: One or two sentences about the game, shown in the This Game tab.
fields.how_to_play: Short instructions, shown in the This Game tab. Keep it to a few sentences.
fields.settings: Optional: up to three on/off switches for your game, shown in the This Game tab below the Sound switch that every game gets. A list of { "label": "Easy / Hard", "default": 0 } entries. The switch's left position is 0 and its right position is 1, so a label written as "Left / Right" lines up with the switch. Keep a label to about 20 characters. default is where the switch starts (0 or 1); after that the app remembers each player's choice on their own device. [] or no settings field = no switches of your own. A fourth entry is ignored. AS THINGS STAND the switches are only shown and remembered: no game can read them, so they change nothing in a game. A setting your game really needs is your game's own job (its own options screen, say).

good_to_know: Every field except folder_name is optional. A missing or empty field falls back to something sensible.

High scores need nothing in this file: a game includes games/game-helper.js and calls Halloween.reportScore(42) at game over; the app keeps the five best per game on the player's device and shows them in the This Game tab. See the top of games/game-helper.js.

The app never pauses a game. The player can open the bottom panel at any time, it covers about the lower half of the game, and the game is not paused or told. A game that needs a pause builds its own. See 1.8 in games/README - game design requirements.md.
